headline: Researchers in China report that a single particle of light was shifted by a controlled amount in a laboratory using a tiny crystal at room temperature, which they say gives a basis for future quantum devices.
score_reason: Peer-reviewed result in a major journal, kept at the pool score; it is a single laboratory demonstration, not a working device.
importance_line: The authors report a basic ingredient of quantum logic and light switching working at room temperature in the lab, which matters first to researchers building light-based quantum chips and later to companies that might use them, but it is one experiment reported by its own authors.
summary: Science Advances published a study by researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences in which a tiny man-made crystal (a colloidal quantum dot) was placed inside a structure that traps light, and the team showed it could shift the timing (the phase) of the light wave of a single photon, a particle of light, by a controlled amount at room temperature. The authors say this gives an experimental basis for future quantum logic gates and very low-power optical switches, but it is a laboratory demonstration and they present it only as a basis for such devices.
notes: Written from the abstract and author list obtained through the Crossref API because science.org returned 403; full paper not read. Original outlet is the same (Science Advances).
